body.statement: For every fixed \(n\ge2\), \(k\ge2\), and \(1\le m\le k-1\), there exist fixed constants \((c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) and distinct smooth positive mechanisms such that the empty-DAG models \(\theta_0,\theta_h\) from Definition \(\mathrm{def:hamiltonian\text{-}lower\text{-}family}\) belong to \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) for every sufficiently small \(h\). The trigonometric contrasts obey the common finite-type margin, have uniformly separated critical points, and attain order \(m\). The perturbation is supported on \(\{|x_{12}|<h\}\times\mathbb T^{n-2}\), preserves \(\lambda^n\) exactly, and satisfies the displayed uniform \(C^k\) envelope for both \(\Psi_h\) and \(\Psi_h^{-1}\). In the case \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), both models also belong to \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}\).
body.justification: Membership must be proved, rather than assumed, so the converse lives in one fixed nondegenerate class.
body.gap: CauCA's plateau rotation does not belong to the finite-type class and does not supply a small nonzero law discrepancy.
body.consumer: This proposition makes the lower modulus applicable to the same bounded class used by the upper theorem.
